prompt: Convert an int (1-3999) to a roman numeral string by looping over an enum whose constants list numeral pieces from largest to smallest. Complete toRoman in RomanNumeral.
explanation: Numeral.values() returns the constants in declaration order, so listing them largest-first turns the conversion into a greedy loop: take as many of each piece as fits, then move on. Including the subtractive pairs (CM, CD, XC, XL, IX, IV) as their own constants means no special-case logic is ever needed -- 900 simply consumes CM before C is considered. name() returns the constant's identifier ('XC'), which doubles as the roman spelling.
hints: values() gives you every constant in the order declared -- largest value first here, which is exactly what a greedy algorithm needs.
For each numeral, use a while loop (not if): 3000 needs M appended three times.
numeral.name() is the string "M", "CM", ... Append to a StringBuilder and subtract getValue() from n each time.
